key_insight: AutoFigure pairs a new large-scale benchmark (FigureBench) with a generation+refinement pipeline to automatically produce publication-ready scientific illustrations from long-form scientific text, reducing the manual burden of figure creation.
problem_solved: Manual creation of high-quality scientific illustrations is time-consuming and expertise-intensive; the paper addresses automatic generation and iterative refinement of figures from long-form scientific text across diverse sources.
method: Introduce FigureBench: a 3,300 high-quality text–figure pair benchmark drawn from papers, surveys, blogs, and other long-form scientific texts for training and evaluation.
Develop AutoFigure: a multimodal generation pipeline that converts descriptive scientific text into initial illustrations.
Apply iterative refinement (layout, visual style, and content grounding) and evaluation modules to produce publication-ready figures and measure quality.
impact: Provides practitioners with a standardized dataset and a practical pipeline to accelerate figure production, enabling faster paper drafting, reproducible visuals, and focused research on text-to-illustration models and refinement techniques.
visual_elements: Dataset snapshot: bar chart/pie showing source breakdown (papers, surveys, blogs) and count = 3,300 pairs
Pipeline diagram: long-form text → generation model → refinement stages → final publication-ready figure
Before/After grid: side-by-side initial vs. refined illustrations for several example inputs
Evaluation dashboard: qualitative/quantitative metrics (readability, fidelity, layout correctness) as small icons/charts
paper_title: AutoFigure: Generating and Refining Publication-Ready Scientific Illustrations
paper_authors: Minjun Zhu, Zhen Lin, Yixuan Weng, Panzhong Lu, Qiujie Xie
